title: Rosalind and the Thorn
premise: Orsen Dunmore, a cartographer of unmapped realms, has spent seven years selling small charms in Thornhollow, a city that outlawed magic after the Sundering War. When a dying stranger presses a living map into her hands, the map pulls her bodily into its ink, binding her to carry a secret: the location of the Heartroot, the source of all magic the city's founders believed destroyed. Hunted by the Wardens who enforce the ban and shadowed by a rebel archivist named Cael who claims the map chose her for a reason, Orsen must decide whether to surrender it and preserve an uneasy peace built on lies, or reveal that magic never died—it was imprisoned, and its prison is failing. As the thirteenth moon wanes, she chooses neither side: she releases the Heartroot's power back into the land itself, dissolving both the Wardens' monopoly and the rebels' cause, at the cost of the map—and the part of herself it claimed.
about_author: Hazel Almeida is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a coastal town where the fog rolls in like a story looking for an ending.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In Thornhollow's night market, Orsen sells harmless charms while hiding her true gift: maps that draw themselves. A bleeding stranger collapses at her stall, presses a folded map into her hands, and dies whispering 'the thirteenth turn.' The map burns cold against her skin. Emotional beat: dread—the past she fled has found her.

chapters.title: Ink That Breathes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The map refuses to be hidden; it redraws itself nightly, showing roads that shouldn't exist. When Warden inspectors raid her lodgings, the map yanks her through its own ink into an unmapped forest. She meets Cael, a rebel archivist tracking the same stranger. Emotional beat: disorientation curdling into wary alliance.

chapters.title: The City of Banned Names
chapters.summary: Cael's POV. He brings Orsen to the Undercroft, rebels hiding beneath Thornhollow, who believe the map leads to the Heartroot. Their leader, Maren, reveals the Sundering War's true history—magic wasn't destroyed but caged. Orsen lies about what the stranger told her. Emotional beat: belonging offered on false pretenses.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Studying the map in secret, Orsen discovers it responds to her blood—a family mark she shares with the dead stranger. Flashbacks reveal her mother was a cartographer executed in the purges. The map shows a thirteenth moon approaching fast. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Door
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A Warden informant exposes the Undercroft. In the raid, Orsen uses the map to pull survivors to safety, revealing her power to everyone—including a captured rebel who will talk. Cael defends her choice; Maren calls it reckless exposure. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by consequence.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Orsen and Cael's POV alternating. Fleeing with the map toward the Heartroot, they travel roads the map creates as they walk. They grow close; Cael confesses he lost his sister to the Wardens' trials. But Orsen learns the map is consuming her memories to fuel itself. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the prison-gate, they find the Wardens already there—not to destroy the Heartroot but to harvest it, sustaining their rule. High Warden Vess offers Orsen a bargain: her mother's name cleared, her freedom, in exchange for the map. The moon reaches its thirteenth turn overhead. Emotional beat: temptation at its sharpest edge.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Ink
chapters.summary: Cael's POV. Maren's rebels arrive to seize the Heartroot by force, and Cael realizes Orsen has been concealing the map's final instruction: it can only be opened by dying. When he tries to stop her from sacrificing herself, the map takes his memories of her instead. Emotional beat: love and betrayal entangled.

chapters.title: The Heartroot
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Inside the prison, Orsen meets the remnant of the stranger—her aunt—who reveals the truth: the map doesn't want a death, it wants a willing cartographer to redraw the world's boundaries. Orsen chooses a third path, releasing the Heartroot into soil and sky rather than any faction's hands. Emotional beat: defiant clarity.

chapters.title: A Map With No Borders
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue-like. Magic returns gently to Thornhollow; the Wardens' charter crumbles without their stolen power, and Maren's rebellion loses its reason to exist. Orsen, missing pieces of herself she may never recover, opens a new shop selling honest maps. Cael arrives, a stranger carrying a feeling he can't name. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal—belonging rebuilt from loss.
